[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Identify parts of the expression using **BODMAS**: Solve **brackets** and **multiplication** first.

Value of bracket (24 + 17) = **41**

Value of multiplication 35 × 2 = **70**

Combine results: 93 − 47 + 69 − 41 + 70 = **144**

**∴ The correct answer is 144.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** 93 − 47 + 69 − (24 + 17) + 35 × 2

Apply **BODMAS** (Bracket, Of, Division, Multiplication, Addition, Subtraction):

Step 1: Solve the parenthesis **(B)**

⇒ 93 − 47 + 69 − 41 + 35 × 2

Step 2: Perform the multiplication **(M)**

⇒ 93 − 47 + 69 − 41 + 70

Step 3: Perform addition and subtraction from left to right **(A/S)**

⇒ 46 + 69 − 41 + 70

⇒ 115 − 41 + 70

⇒ 74 + 70

⇒ 144

**∴ The correct answer is 144.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

BODMAS Hierarchy

Mathematical operations must follow the priority: **Brackets** → **Orders** (powers/roots) → **Division** → **Multiplication** → **Addition** → **Subtraction**.

VBODMAS Rule

In complex simplifications, **V** stands for **Vinculum** (bar bracket), which is solved even before standard brackets.

Sign Rules

When multiplying signs: (−) × (−) = (+), (+) × (−) = (−), and (−) × (+) = (−).

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Solve **multiplication** and **division** terms first: (27 × 1) = 27 and 39 ÷ 3 = 13.

Rewrite the expression: 92 + 27 − 41 + 13 + 21 − 17.

Sum all **positive numbers**: 92 + 27 + 13 + 21 = 153.

Sum all **negative numbers**: 41 + 17 = 58.

Final value: 153 − 58 = 95.

**∴ The correct answer is 95.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** 92 + (27 × 1) − 41 + 39 ÷ 3 + 21 − 17

**Method:** Apply the **BODMAS** rule (Brackets, Orders, Division, Multiplication, Addition, Subtraction).

⇒ 92 + 27 − 41 + 39 ÷ 3 + 21 − 17 (Solving **Bracket**: 27 × 1)

⇒ 92 + 27 − 41 + 13 + 21 − 17 (Solving **Division**: 39 ÷ 3)

⇒ 119 − 41 + 13 + 21 − 17 (Solving **Addition** from left: 92 + 27)

⇒ 78 + 13 + 21 − 17 (Solving **Subtraction**: 119 − 41)

⇒ 91 + 21 − 17 (Solving **Addition**: 78 + 13)

⇒ 112 − 17 (Solving **Addition**: 91 + 21)

⇒ 95 (Final **Subtraction**)

**∴ The correct answer is 95.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

BODMAS Rule

It stands for **Brackets**, **Orders**, **Division**, **Multiplication**, **Addition**, and **Subtraction**, defining the correct sequence for solving arithmetic operations.

Left-to-Right Associativity

When operations like **addition** and **subtraction** (or division and multiplication) appear together, they are generally performed in the order they appear from left to right.

questions.question: Find the HCF and LCM of the fractions 3/8, 5/12, and 7/18.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For any set of **fractions**:

**HCF** = HCF(Numerators) ÷ LCM(Denominators) = HCF(3, 5, 7) ÷ LCM(8, 12, 18) = 1/72

**LCM** = LCM(Numerators) ÷ HCF(Denominators) = LCM(3, 5, 7) ÷ HCF(8, 12, 18) = 105/2

**∴ The correct answer is HCF = 1/72, LCM = 105/2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given Fractions:** 3/8, 5/12, and 7/18

**Formula Used:**

1. **HCF of Fractions** = HCF of Numerators ÷ LCM of Denominators

2. **LCM of Fractions** = LCM of Numerators ÷ HCF of Denominators

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/151e32ab072c7fdd10226c32eea718da149602d0a81e9280007139cf6e642bfc.png] 

**Step-by-step Calculations:**

⇒ **Numerators** = 3, 5, 7

⇒ **Denominators** = 8, 12, 18

⇒ HCF(3, 5, 7) = 1 (Since they are **co-prime** numbers)

⇒ LCM(3, 5, 7) = 3 × 5 × 7 = 105

⇒ LCM(8, 12, 18):

⇒ 8 = 2³

⇒ 12 = 2² × 3

⇒ 18 = 2 × 3²

⇒ **LCM** = 2³ × 3² = 8 × 9 = 72

⇒ HCF(8, 12, 18) = 2 (Highest common factor among 8, 12, and 18)

⇒ **HCF of Fractions** = 1/72

⇒ **LCM of Fractions** = 105/2

**∴ The correct answer is HCF = 1/72, LCM = 105/2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

HCF of Fractions

To find the **Highest Common Factor** of fractions, calculate HCF(Numerators) ÷ LCM(Denominators). Ensure fractions are in simplest form.

LCM of Fractions

To find the **Least Common Multiple** of fractions, calculate LCM(Numerators) ÷ HCF(Denominators).

Co-prime Numbers

If a set of numbers are **co-prime** (like 3, 5, 7), their HCF is always 1 and their LCM is their product.

questions.question: If x=sqrt{289}times sqrt{225}+sqrt{144}, then what is the value of 2x?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Solve for **square roots**: √289 = 17, √225 = 15, and √144 = 12.

Calculate x: x = (17 × 15) + 12 = 255 + 12 = 267.

Calculate the required value: 2x = 2 × 267 = 534.

**∴ The correct answer is 534.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Expression: x = √289 × √225 + √144

**Method Used:**

Apply **BODMAS** rule and basic **Square Roots** calculation.

**Calculations:**

⇒ x = 17 × 15 + 12

⇒ x = 255 + 12

⇒ x = 267

⇒ 2x = 2 × 267

⇒ 2x = 534

**∴ The correct answer is 534.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

BODMAS Rule

The acronym stands for **Brackets, Orders (Powers and Roots), Division, Multiplication, Addition, and Subtraction**. It defines the order of operations to solve complex arithmetic expressions.

Perfect Squares

Numbers like 289, 225, and 144 are **perfect squares**. Memorizing squares up to 30 (e.g., 17² = 289, 15² = 225, 12² = 144) is essential for fast calculations in competitive exams.

Simplification Shortcut

When multiplying numbers ending in 5 (like 17 × 15), use the property (16 + 1)(16 − 1) = 16² − 1 = 256 − 1 = 255 for quicker results.

**∴ The correct answer is 7/3.**

questions.question: The breadth of a rectangular hall is 4/5 of its length. The area of the floor is 320 square metre, then what is the difference (in metre) between the length and breadth of the hall?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of **Length** : **Breadth** = 5 : 4 (since Breadth = 4/5 of Length).

Product of ratio units = 5 × 4 = 20 units².

20 units² = 320 m² ⇒ 1 unit² = 16 m² ⇒ 1 unit = 4 m.

Difference between **Length** and **Breadth** = (5 − 4) = 1 unit.

Difference = 1 × 4 = 4 m.

**∴ The correct answer is 4 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Breadth** (B) = 4/5 × **Length** (L)

**Area** of the floor = 320 m²

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0ee847d7140fd607af5df5aa4f8cc25e2b405d44a3ec66be80194205dd40cbde.png] 

Let the **Length** be 5x and the **Breadth** be 4x.

⇒ **Area** = **Length** × **Breadth**

⇒ 320 = 5x × 4x

⇒ 320 = 20x²

⇒ x² = 320 ÷ 20

⇒ x² = 16

⇒ x = √16 = 4 m

⇒ **Length** = 5 × 4 = 20 m

⇒ **Breadth** = 4 × 4 = 16 m

⇒ **Difference** = 20 m − 16 m = 4 m.

**∴ The correct answer is 4 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Area of a Rectangle

The total space occupied by the rectangle is calculated as **Area** = **Length** × **Breadth**.

Perimeter of a Rectangle

The total boundary length is given by **Perimeter** = 2 × (**Length** + **Breadth**).

Diagonal of a Rectangle

The distance between opposite corners is found using **Diagonal** = √(**Length**² + **Breadth**²).

questions.question: (325 - 275)² + 4 × 325 × 275 = ?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Recognize the **algebraic identity**: (a − b)² + 4ab = (a + b)².

Here, **a = 325** and **b = 275**.

Sum of values: 325 + 275 = **600**.

Simplified result: 600² = **360000**.

**∴ The correct answer is 360000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given values:** a = 325, b = 275.

**Method Used:** Identity expansion and simplification.

⇒ (325 − 275)² + 4 × 325 × 275

⇒ Let a = 325 and b = 275.

⇒ The expression is in the form: (a − b)² + 4ab.

⇒ (a² + b² − 2ab) + 4ab

⇒ a² + b² + 2ab = (a + b)².

⇒ (325 + 275)²

⇒ 600² = 360000.

**∴ The correct answer is 360000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Basic Square Identities

Standard expansions for binomial squares: (a + b)² = a² + b² + 2ab and (a − b)² = a² + b² − 2ab.

Difference and Sum Square Relation

Conversion formula between the sum and difference of squares: (a + b)² − (a − b)² = 4ab.

Sum of Squared Terms

Addition identity for combined squares: (a + b)² + (a − b)² = 2(a² + b²).

questions.question: The difference between the length and breadth of a rectangle is 10 metres. If its perimeter is 140 metres, then what will be the area (in square metre) of rectangle?

questions.question: The average weight of A, B and C is 30 kg. The average weight of A and B is 32 kg. The average weight of B and C is 38 kg. What is the weight (in kg) of B?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Weight of B** = [Sum of group 1 + Sum of group 2] − [Total sum]

Sum of **A and B** = 32 × 2 = 64 kg

Sum of **B and C** = 38 × 2 = 76 kg

Sum of **A, B and C** = 30 × 3 = 90 kg

**Weight of B** = (64 + 76) − 90 = 140 − 90 = 50 kg

**∴ The correct answer is 50 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Average weight** of (A + B + C) = 30 kg

**Average weight** of (A + B) = 32 kg

**Average weight** of (B + C) = 38 kg

**Formula Used:**

**Total Weight** = Average Weight × Number of Persons

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/93f9f98a36a18f6e4a7a4f1be9356c4ffbe8a9d7a32761ecc8c056dfdbb7ee3a.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ **Total weight** of A + B + C = 30 × 3 = 90 kg --- (i)

⇒ **Total weight** of A + B = 32 × 2 = 64 kg --- (ii)

⇒ **Total weight** of B + C = 38 × 2 = 76 kg --- (iii)

⇒ Adding (ii) and (iii): (A + B) + (B + C) = 64 + 76

⇒ A + 2B + C = 140 kg --- (iv)

⇒ Subtracting (i) from (iv): (A + 2B + C) − (A + B + C) = 140 − 90

⇒ **Weight of B** = 50 kg

**∴ The correct answer is 50 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Definition of Average

The **average** (Arithmetic Mean) is the sum of all values divided by the total number of values. Formula: **Average** = Sum of observations ÷ Number of observations.

Net Deviation Method

The sum of deviations of all values from the **average** is always zero. This is useful for finding missing values in a data set when the average is known.

Combined Average

If two groups have **n₁** and **n₂** elements with averages **A₁** and **A₂**, the combined average is [n₁A₁ + n₂A₂] ÷ [n₁ + n₂].

questions.question: The average of 100 numbers is 53.5. By addition of 50 new numbers, the average becomes 74.1. What is the sum of newly added numbers?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total numbers increased by **50** (from **100** to **150**) and the average increased by **20.6** (74.1 − 53.5).

Sum of new numbers = (New Average × Quantity of new numbers) + (Old Quantity × Increase in Average)

Sum = (74.1 × 50) + (100 × 20.6)

Sum = 3705 + 2060 = 5765

**∴ The correct answer is 5765.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial count (n₁) = **100**, Initial average (A₁) = **53.5**

New added count (n₂) = **50**, Total count (nₜₒₜₐₗ) = **150**

Final average (Aₜₒₜₐₗ) = **74.1**

**Formula Used:**

Sum = Average × Number of terms

Sum of new numbers = (Total Sum of 150 numbers) − (Initial Sum of 100 numbers)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2a82f0182387614b6e37bdc804a0fba78a5f3b29789e41527010f0b6778eff44.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Initial Sum = 100 × 53.5 = 5350

⇒ Total Sum after adding 50 numbers = 150 × 74.1

⇒ Total Sum = 11115

⇒ Sum of 50 newly added numbers = 11115 − 5350

⇒ Sum = 5765

**∴ The correct answer is 5765.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Weighted Average Formula

When two groups are combined, the combined average is (n₁A₁ + n₂A₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).

Effect of Adding/Removing a Term

If a new value X is added to a group of n terms with average A, the new average A′ = (nA + X) ÷ (n + 1).

Sum of First n Natural Numbers

The sum is given by [n(n + 1)] ÷ 2, and their average is (n + 1) ÷ 2.

questions.question: The traffic lights at three different road crossings change after every 30 seconds, 45 seconds and 60 seconds respectively. If they all change simultaneously at 7:00 a.m., then find the time (in a.m.) at which they will change simultaneously again?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

To find the next simultaneous change, calculate the **LCM** of the given intervals: 30, 45, and 60 seconds.

**LCM**(30, 45, 60) = 180 seconds.

Convert 180 seconds to minutes: 180 ÷ 60 = **3 minutes**.

Add 3 minutes to the initial time **7:00 a.m.** → **7:03 a.m.**

**∴ The correct answer is 7:03 a.m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Interval of Light 1 = **30 seconds**

Interval of Light 2 = **45 seconds**

Interval of Light 3 = **60 seconds**

Starting Time = **7:00 a.m.**

**Formula Used:**

Next simultaneous event = Initial time + **LCM**(Intervals)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7f0358c230d267be1d81753f55a629b1afbd4a14b868b7a31cf130ace4528f77.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Prime factors of 30 = 2 × 3 × 5

⇒ Prime factors of 45 = 3² × 5

⇒ Prime factors of 60 = 2² × 3 × 5

⇒ **LCM**(30, 45, 60) = 2² × 3² × 5

⇒ **LCM** = 4 × 9 × 5 = **180 seconds**

⇒ Time in minutes = 180 ÷ 60 = **3 minutes**

⇒ Next simultaneous change = 7:00 a.m. + 3 minutes = **7:03 a.m.**

**∴ The correct answer is 7:03 a.m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Concept of LCM

The **Least Common Multiple (LCM)** is used to find the next time periodic events (like bells, traffic lights, or racing laps) will occur simultaneously.

Time Conversion

Always ensure units are consistent. Use **1 minute = 60 seconds** to convert large second counts into readable time formats.

Relationship between HCF and LCM

For any two numbers a and b: **HCF(a, b) × LCM(a, b) = a × b**.

questions.question: Selling price of an article is Rs. 5625. Profit percentage is 25 percent. What is the cost price of the article?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Profit** 25% = 1/4 (Fractional value)

Ratio of **Cost Price** (CP) : **Selling Price** (SP) = 4 : (4 + 1) = 4 : 5

Given 5 units (SP) = ₹5625 ⇒ 1 unit = 5625 ÷ 5 = ₹1125

CP = 4 units = 4 × 1125 = ₹4500

**∴ The correct answer is ₹4500.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Selling Price** (SP) = ₹5625

**Profit percentage** = 25%

**Formula Used:**

Cost Price (CP) = [Selling Price × 100] ÷ [100 + Profit %]

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/621e1a506a836d5dbee5d341d4da7699cde8201eaf14552a444f4541cf62d3df.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ CP = [5625 × 100] ÷ [100 + 25]

⇒ CP = [5625 × 100] ÷ 125

⇒ CP = 5625 ÷ 1.25

⇒ CP = ₹4500

**∴ The correct answer is ₹4500.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Cost Price with Loss

When there is a loss, CP = [SP × 100] ÷ [100 − Loss %].

Profit/Loss Basis

Profit or Loss is always calculated on the **Cost Price** unless otherwise specified in the question.

Marked Price (MP)

MP = CP + Markup. Selling Price is also calculated as MP − Discount.

questions.question: A is 20 percent less than B. If value of A is 480, then what is the value of B?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Convert **percentage** to **ratio**: 20% = 1/5

If **B** is 5 units, then **A** is (5 − 1) = 4 units.

Given **A** = 480 ⇒ 4 units = 480

1 unit = 480 ÷ 4 = 120

**B** = 5 units = 5 × 120 = 600

**∴ The correct answer is 600.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Value of **A** = 480

**A** is **20 percent less** than **B**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/390f0ce99184832eee183d3ed66af74ffbd8ffe4243611fa2dc2682ae1edec8f.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Value = Base × (100 − % Decrease) ÷ 100

**Calculations:**

⇒ **A** = **B** × (100 − 20) ÷ 100

⇒ 480 = **B** × (80 ÷ 100)

⇒ 480 = **B** × 0.8

⇒ **B** = 480 ÷ 0.8

⇒ **B** = 4800 ÷ 8

⇒ **B** = 600

**∴ The correct answer is 600.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Percentage to Fraction Conversion

To simplify calculations, memorize common fractions: 20% = 1/5, 25% = 1/4, 33.33% = 1/3, and 50% = 1/2.

Percentage Increase/Decrease

New Value = Original Value × (1 ± r/100), where 'r' is the rate of **percentage change**.

Inverse Percentage Relation

If A is x% less than B, then B is [x / (100 − x)] × 100% more than A. In this case, B is 25% more than A.

questions.question: If 30 percent of 500 is 50 percent more than A, then what is the value of A?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Calculate the first value: **30%** of **500** = 150.

Express **50% more than A** as a multiplier: 100% + 50% = 150% or **1.5**.

Set up the equation: 1.5 × **A** = 150 ⇒ **A** = 150 ÷ 1.5 = 100.

**∴ The correct answer is 100.**

questions.question: A person earns 30 percent profit on selling price. What is the ratio of the value of the profit to the cost price of the article?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Profit** is 30% of **Selling Price (SP)**, which equals 3/10.

Let **SP** = 10 units, then **Profit** = 3 units.

**Cost Price (CP)** = **SP** − **Profit** = 10 − 3 = 7 units.

Required **Ratio** of **Profit** to **CP** = 3 : 7.

**∴ The correct answer is 3 : 7.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Profit** = 30% of the **Selling Price (SP)**.

**Formula Used:**

**Cost Price (CP)** = **Selling Price (SP)** − **Profit**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4dabfc5453fe3d07c7dbd77b5f5a26c16e0a04110dc101d8b89189a09cbd9ab9.png] 

⇒ Let the **Selling Price (SP)** of the article be ₹100.

⇒ **Profit** = 30% of ₹100 = (30/100) × 100 = ₹30.

⇒ **Cost Price (CP)** = **SP** − **Profit**

⇒ **CP** = 100 − 30 = ₹70.

⇒ **Ratio** of **Profit** to **Cost Price** = 30 : 70

⇒ **Ratio** = 3 : 7.

**∴ The correct answer is 3 : 7.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Profit Percentage on Cost Price

Usually, profit is calculated on **CP**. Profit % = (Profit ÷ **CP**) × 100.

Selling Price Formula

**SP** = **CP** × (100 + **Profit%**) ÷ 100, where **Profit%** is based on the **Cost Price**.

Relationship between SP, CP, and Profit

When **SP** > **CP**, there is a profit. **Profit** = **SP** − **CP**.

questions.question: P and Q together can complete a work in 8 days. R alone can complete the same work in 16 days. P, Q and R together can complete 1/2 part of the same work in how many days?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total work = LCM of **8** and **16** = 16 units.

Efficiency of **(P + Q)** = 16 ÷ 8 = 2 units/day.

Efficiency of **R** = 16 ÷ 16 = 1 unit/day.

Combined efficiency of **(P + Q + R)** = 2 + 1 = 3 units/day.

Time for **1/2 part** of work = (16 ÷ 2) ÷ 3 = 8/3 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 8/3 days.**

questions.question: Total length of train A and train B is 800 metres. These trains are running in opposite direction. Total speed of train A and train B is 40 m/s. In how much time (in seconds) these trains will cross each other?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When two objects move in **opposite directions**, their **relative speed** is the sum of their individual speeds.

Relative Speed = 40 m/s

Total distance to cover = Sum of lengths of **Train A** and **Train B** = 800 m.

Time = Total Distance ÷ Relative Speed = 800 ÷ 40 = 20 seconds.

**∴ The correct answer is 20 sec.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Sum of lengths (L₁ + L₂) = 800 m

Sum of speeds (SA + SB) = 40 m/s

**Formula Used:**

Time (t) = Total Distance ÷ Relative Speed

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/fb1e9dd326ea328f51f914f3337f2943d67ce8e29d2aca5b47c2b926c91e6703.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total Distance = 800 m

⇒ Relative Speed = 40 m/s

⇒ Crossing Time (t) = 800 ÷ 40

⇒ t = 20 sec

**∴ The correct answer is 20 sec.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed Concept

When two objects move in **opposite directions**, the relative speed is the sum (S₁ + S₂). If they move in the **same direction**, the relative speed is the difference (|S₁ − S₂|).

Crossing Criteria

When a train crosses a **pole or a man**, distance equals the length of the train. When it crosses a **bridge or platform**, distance equals (Length of train + Length of platform).

Unit Conversion

To convert **km/hr to m/s**, multiply by 5/18. To convert **m/s to km/hr**, multiply by 18/5.

questions.question: A train crosses a standing man in 4 seconds. This train also crosses a 'y' metre long platform in 12 seconds at the same speed. What will be the ratio of length of train to the total length of train and platform?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When speed is **constant**, the **Distance** covered is directly proportional to the **Time** taken.

Time to cover **Train Length** (L) = 4 sec

Time to cover **Total Length** (Train + Platform) = 12 sec

Required Ratio = 4 : 12

⇒ Ratio = 1 : 3

**∴ The correct answer is 1 : 3.**
